title: A Salt for the Crown Revisited
premise: Zephyrine Yarrow, a mercenary bound by an oath to a god who has not spoken in thirty years, keeps accounts for the Gildhall of Impossible Things—trades in forgotten names, bottled griefs, and debts owed across realms. When a feral child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Zephyrine discovers the child is the living remnant of the covenant her god died sealing, and that the silence she has mourned was never abandonment but sacrifice. To reforge the broken covenant between the mortal world and the realm of the silent god, Zephyrine must trade the one thing the Gildhall forbids: a memory freely given, her own. She pays it, becoming a stranger to her own past, and in doing so restores the god's voice—but the final chapter reveals she chose this trade once before, long ago, and the ledger's oldest entry bears her own handwriting.
about_author: B. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging ship manifests and salvage claims before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ledgers, oaths, and the people who keep accounts that kingdoms would rather see burned.

chapters.title: The Weight of Uncounted Things
chapters.summary: Zephyrine balances the Gildhall's ledgers while quietly grieving her god's thirty-year silence. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a hollow faith; she audits a trade in a bottled grief and feels nothing, which frightens her.

chapters.title: A Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A mud-caked girl appears at the Gildhall door speaking a language no living scholar knows. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: recognition and dread—the words make the ledger ink crawl, and Zephyrine's oath-mark burns for the first time in decades.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Writes Back
chapters.summary: Zephyrine discovers the child's speech is transcribing itself into the Gildhall's oldest ledger. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: vertigo as she reads an entry describing her own arrival at the Gildhall, written before she was born.

chapters.title: Debts of the Silent God
chapters.summary: Gildmaster Corvane reveals the child is called a Remnant—a fragment of the covenant her god died sealing. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism hiding fear; Corvane orders the child cataloged as inventory, and Zephyrine refuses.

chapters.title: What the Gildhall Forbids
chapters.summary: Zephyrine learns the Gildhall's one law: no memory may be traded freely given, because freely given memories are how covenants are sealed. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: dawning understanding of why her god went silent—and what reforging will cost.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Oath
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitors arrive seeking the child, calling her an abomination. POV: Inquisitor Dain Maret. Emotional beat: righteous certainty beginning to crack as Maret witnesses the child heal a dying sparrow with a word.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Salt Marshes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine flees with the child, pursued by Maret's riders. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: fierce protectiveness she didn't know she possessed; the child begins speaking words Zephyrine's oath-mark translates in her dreams.

chapters.title: The Chapel of No Answer
chapters.summary: They shelter in the ruined chapel where Zephyrine swore her oath. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief and anger as she demands her god answer; the child touches the altar and the silence, for one heartbeat, breaks.

chapters.title: A Word Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: The child speaks Zephyrine's true name in the old tongue, and memories not her own flood in. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness intertwined—she glimpses the god's final day and understands the child is both messenger and key.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To reach the realm of the silent god, they must trade passage with the Ferryman of the Gildhall's founding. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: bargaining desperation; the Ferryman names his price—one memory, freely given—and Zephyrine lies and says she'll pay later.

chapters.title: Maret's Doubt
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maret finds them but hesitates, having uncovered evidence the Crown engineered the covenant's breaking. POV: Maret. Emotional beat: crisis of faith; he lets them pass, becoming a hunted man himself.

chapters.title: Corvane's Gambit
chapters.summary: Gildmaster Corvane, seeking to monopolize the covenant, sells their route to the Crown. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into paranoia as he realizes the ledgers have begun writing entries he cannot read.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and the child descend into a submerged vault holding the covenant's original terms. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: awe and horror—she reads the clause requiring a freely given memory, and recognizes the signature already on it: her own.

chapters.title: Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: A memory chapter: Zephyrine relives, via the child's touch, the night she first sealed the covenant and chose to forget. POV: alternating Zephyrine/child. Emotional beat: shattering revelation—her god's silence was the price of her own forgetting.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Corvane and Crown soldiers ambush them at the river crossing. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: rage and sacrifice; Maret dies holding the ford so they can escape, and Zephyrine carries his name to the ledger.

chapters.title: The God Who Chose Silence
chapters.summary: At the threshold between realms, the child speaks the whole truth: the god went silent to hold the realms apart, and only a freely given memory can reforge what broke. POV: the child. Emotional beat: innocent sorrow—the child knows she will cease to exist when the covenant mends.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Corvane attempts to seal the covenant himself with a stolen memory, and the ledger rejects him, unmaking his trades. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: ruin—everything he hoarded returns to its owners, leaving him with nothing but his own name, which he no longer recognizes.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: At the covenant's broken heart, Zephyrine offers her memory—her whole past—freely given. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: quiet resolve and grief; the god's voice returns through her sacrifice, and the child begins to dissolve into the mended whole.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Ledger
chapters.summary: The covenant restored, Zephyrine wakes at the Gildhall with no past, and the god speaks to her for the first time. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: disorientation turning to peace—she is a stranger to herself, but not to her purpose.

chapters.title: The Oldest Entry
chapters.summary: Rebuilding her life entry by entry, Zephyrine finds the ledger's first page bears her handwriting, dated a century before her birth. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: wonder edged with unease—the cycle is older than she knew, and she wrote the beginning.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: The child's echo survives as a new word in the old tongue meaning 'belonging.' Zephyrine teaches it to the Gildhall. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: bittersweet healing; justice was never the Crown's to give—it lived in the trade freely made.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Crown
chapters.summary: Years later, a mud-caked traveler arrives at the Gildhall door speaking a language no living scholar knows. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: recognition without memory—she opens the ledger to a fresh page, and her hand already knows what to write.
